mechanism_claims.claim_text: PA-13 damages P. aeruginosa membranes by inducing permeability and membrane-potential disruption in a dose- and time-dependent flow-cytometry assay.
direct_assay_types: dose/time response at 1x MIC and 0.5x MIC

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=28:Membrane permeability and depolarization; xml:fig=6:Figure 6; supp:Fig S4

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism support is in vitro and specific to tested P. aeruginosa conditions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: TAMRA-labelled PA-13 binds to and penetrates P. aeruginosa cells rapidly, with flow-cytometry and confocal microscopy support.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TAMRA-labelled PA-13 against P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853
mechanism_claims.limitations: TAMRA-labelled peptide is a labelled analogue; source states labelled PA-13 was used to localize/track penetration.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Electron microscopy shows PA-13-treated P. aeruginosa with membrane roughening, pores, leakage, and intracellular disruption.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=30:Scanning and transmission electron microscopy; xml:fig=9:Figure 9; xml:fig=10:Figure 10

mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology supports membrane disruption but does not by itself quantify lethal dose-response.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PA-13 binds LPS and inhibits LPS-mediated TLR4 activation in dose-dependent in vitro assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PA-13 with E. coli O111:B4 LPS and P. aeruginosa LPS-mediated hTLR4 stimulation
mechanism_claims.limitations: Anti-inflammatory activity is in vitro; no in vivo efficacy or safety result is claimed.
